page.layout: One printed page: one column of Latin verse, set in stanzas; a marginal note "Sic" in the right margin beside the last stanza. Page number at head centre.

main_text.p:
Turba insolentum, certa manet tamen
Prolis beatæ & innocentis
Spes Deus, & solidum leuamen.

Meos at error pene fefellerat
Gressus, dolebam, quod male pertinax
Sors cuncta misceret benignè,
Quæ cuperent stolidè superbi.

Nam nulla fati dira necessitas
Hos tangit unquam: sed velut ardua
Fundata firmis arx columnis,
Mole sua mala quæq; frangunt.

Et certa quæ nos perpetuò manet
Sors, qui gementes incolimus breuem
Vitam, ut malis exerceamur,
Hos onerat quoq; sæua nunquam.

Hinc efferunt tantos quoq; spiritus,
Quæcunq; mente inflatius asserunt
Vt summa iactent, cæterorum
Præq; suis pia facta temnant.

Et impotenti sunt quoq; turgidi
Fastu, intumescunt præ nimio malo,
Et perpetrant quodcunq; tandem
Mens agitat malesuada crimen.

Carpunt superbè quælibet, intonant
Ex alto, & omnes despiciunt bonos:
Sed quicquid illi dictitarint,
Lege volunt stabili teneri.Sic

page.notes:
Verse printed as stanzas of four lines; the first stanza has three lines on this page and continues from the previous page. The marginal note "Sic" stands beside the last line of the page. No running head, catchword or signature printed. Line breaks within stanzas are marked with
. Printed forms kept: "male", "misceret", "benignè", "stolidè", "perpetuò", "quoq;", "quæcunq;" and "Lege volunt" (printed as one word, "Legeuolunt", read as two).
